gerekce: The report supports alinmaz on degerleme_desteksiz independently of the three inputs. Three methodologically distinct valuation angles all point the same way on reconciled TTM operands: 38.92x parent earnings, 30.89x lease-exclusive EV to reported operating income, and a 1.39% parent free-cash-flow yield. These are not one claim in three forms — earnings yield is excluded as the acknowledged inverse of P/E, but the EBIT and cash-flow bases are separate operands with their own reconciliations in Section 4. Against that price, the operating picture offers no offset the report can substantiate: current-quarter free cash flow turned negative at -1,946.0 million USD from +425.0 million USD, operating cash flow and cash conversion are both classified adverse, and the current ratio of 0.77x sits below the 0.93x peer median. The favorable items are real and I weighed them — revenue +7.3%, net income +18.3%, Piotroski 7/9 — but the report embeds no forward estimates, so nothing in it converts single-digit-to-teens growth on a low-single-digit cash yield into a testable thesis at this multiple. That is the definition of an unsupported valuation rather than a business objection, so no thesis is issued and no thesis-breaking conditions apply. The three assessments converged on the same verdict and reason code, and the overlap in their cited numbers with mine is a consequence of the report having few valuation facts, not deference. A's discipline was the cleanest and is the reason I kept the EV/EBIT angle explicitly in my evidence — it was the only assessment to cite it, and it is the one observation that keeps the case from resting on a single earnings claim. B and C reached high confidence partly on characterizations the report contradicts — B's 'low-growth' framing and C's capex-only causal story — which is why I neither adopted their reasoning nor let their stated confidence raise mine; my yuksek rests on the three independent multiples and the reconciliations behind them. C's thesis-breaking conditions were disregarded as structurally inconsistent with its own verdict.
